title: Introduce lightweight RAG playbook templates for edge SDKs and local prober
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Context: Customers building lightweight clients for edge devices requested compact RAG playbooks that are small, deterministic, and instrumented for local telemetry and offline testing. This PR adds a minimal playbook manifest (playbook.v1), two language examples (Node.js and Rust), an opinionated local prober that simulates network/latency/kv-cache behavior, and a concise docs page with runbook and telemetry guidance. Motivation: Many quickstarts focus on cloud-hosted scenarios; developers targeting edge devices need reproducible, small-footprint templates that surface guidance for batching, prefix caching, and OTLP-compatible telemetry. What this PR does: 1) Adds quickstarts/edge-playbooks with a compact YAML manifest (playbook.v1) that supports: - model: reference to model family and quantization profile - routing: local (edge) vs remote (hosted) fallbacks - probes: health and synthetic query harness - cache_policy: prefix/KV cache hints 2) Introduces scripts/local-prober which implements a tiny harness (Rust binary) that can: - run synthetic workload with configurable sequence length distribution - emit OTLP spans/metrics to a collector (localhost by default) - overlay packet-loss and latency profiles to validate graceful degradation 3) Adds examples/nodejs/agent.js showing how to load playbook.v1 and wire the Redwood SDK for edge usage with small-batch settings and memory-conscious KV cache management 4) Adds docs/rag/edge-playbooks.md with quickstart steps, recommended tuning knobs, and a checklist for shipping to constrained devices Testing and CI: - Added ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml that runs unit smoke tests for the playbook parser and the Node example inside a slim Node 18 container - The Rust prober is built in CI and run once with the default smoke profile - All checks passed in this run; full e2e (requires GPUs) is documented but gated behind a manual job Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/edge-playbooks/README.md: overview and getting started - quickstarts/edge-playbooks/templates/playbook.yaml: compact manifest with examples - quickstarts/edge-playbooks/examples/nodejs/agent.js: minimal agent wiring + sample prompts - quickstarts/edge-playbooks/examples/rust/prober.rs: local prober harness and OTLP exporter - docs/rag/edge-playbooks.md: docs site page with knobs and telemetry section - ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml: CI smoke workflow - scripts/local-prober/README.md: how to build/run the prober Usage notes / runbook: - To try locally: 1) Start an OTLP collector (or run `collector --dev`) 2) cd quickstarts/edge-playbooks && npm install && node examples/nodejs/agent.js --playbook templates/playbook.yaml 3) In another terminal build/run the prober: cargo run --bin local-prober -- --profile light --otlp-endpoint http://localhost:4318 - Telemetry: prober emits metrics:edge.probe.latency_ms and traces with span attribute playbook.name. The docs page contains Grafana dashboard JSON to import for quick inspection Rollout plan: - Merge to main; staged docs deploy to staging docs site; announce in #dev-quickstarts and include a short demo script for solutions engineers Backward compatibility and gradual migration: - playbook.v1 is additive and small; existing quickstarts unaffected. The playbook parser will accept legacy playbooks and emit a deprecation warning when an old field is used.

release_notes: Adds edge-focused RAG playbooks and a local prober harness; includes Node.js and Rust examples, OTLP-compatible telemetry, and a CI smoke workflow. Recommended for teams building on-device or constrained-network deployments.
notes: This PR is intentionally additive and intended to seed further examples (Python and Go clients planned). The prober is marked experimental and lives under scripts/local-prober. Solutions engineers asked for a compact template, so this is targeted to reduce onboarding friction for edge customers.
